section: President of India – Election, Term, Impeachment and Powers
sub: Qualifications, Term, Re-election, Oath, Resignation, Emoluments (Arts. 56–60)

section: President of India – Election, Term, Impeachment and Powers
sub: Powers of the President
text: Union executive: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers and Attorney General (Part V, Chapter I) – not the Speaker or the RS Deputy Chairman.

section: President of India – Election, Term, Impeachment and Powers
sub: Powers of the President
text: Reports laid before Parliament by the President: Finance Commission recommendations (Art. 281), CAG reports (Art. 151), National Commission for SCs (Art. 338), UPSC, Linguistic Minorities – but not the PAC report (a committee of Parliament itself).

section: President of India – Election, Term, Impeachment and Powers
sub: Vacancy and Acting President (Arts. 62, 65)

section: Cabinet System, Cabinet Committees, Collective and Individual Responsibility; Attorney General of India
sub: Attorney General of India – Article 76 and Article 88
text: Article 76: office of the Attorney General (AG) for India – the highest (first) law officer of the country; appointed by the President (not by Parliament, the Speaker, the PM or on Parliament's recommendation). Not Arts. 77, 78 or 79.

section: Cabinet System, Cabinet Committees, Collective and Individual Responsibility; Attorney General of India
sub: Attorney General of India – Article 76 and Article 88
text: Article 88: though not a member, he may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House, a joint sitting and any committee of which he is named a member – without a right to vote. So he is the non-member who can participate in Lok Sabha proceedings (not the CJI, the Vice-President, the Solicitor General, the CAG or a Governor).

section: Cabinet System, Cabinet Committees, Collective and Individual Responsibility; Attorney General of India
sub: Attorney General of India – Article 76 and Article 88
text: R. Venkataramani – AG since 1 October 2022 (after K.K. Venugopal); re-appointed for two years from 1 October 2025 (as of 2026).

section: Cabinet System, Cabinet Committees, Collective and Individual Responsibility; Attorney General of India
sub: Cabinet Secretariat, Cabinet Secretary and Chief Secretary
text: Cabinet Secretary: the senior-most / highest civil servant (bureaucrat) of the Union – not the Home Secretary, the PM's Secretary, the Lok Sabha Secretary-General, a Chief Secretary or the Attorney General (a law officer, not a civil servant). "First among equals" among Secretaries; 11th in the Table of Precedence; chairs the Civil Services Board.

sub: Cabinet Committees, Business Rules and Reports on the Machinery of Government

section: Indian Political Parties – Evolution, Ideology and Classification

text: Asked as: number of national parties (6, as of 2025); "more than 10 national parties" (false); recognition provision in the Constitution (false); symbol not bicycle (RJD); BSP elephant.

section: Recognition of National and State Parties – Criteria and the Symbols Order

section: Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
sub: Part XV and the Right to Vote – Articles 324-329, Adult Suffrage
text: Elections are in Part XV (not XIV, XVI or XVII). Correct pair: ECI – Art. 324 (Supreme Court = 124, UPSC = 315, Attorney General = 76); Art. 280 = Finance Commission; Art. 171 = Legislative Councils, not elections.

section: Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
sub: Part XV and the Right to Vote – Articles 324-329, Adult Suffrage
text: ECI set up on 25 January 1950 – permanent constitutional body; its institute IIIDEM trains election managers. Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978): Art. 324 is a "reservoir of power" where Parliament has not legislated.

section: Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
sub: General Elections – Dates, Firsts and Records
text: Shyam Saran Negi (Kalpa, Kinnaur, HP): independent India's first voter (Oct 1951), voted in every general election till 2022; honoured by CEC Navin Chawla (2010).

section: Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
sub: Delimitation – Commission, Freeze and Amendments
text: Delimitation = fixing the number and boundaries of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies, and the SC/ST reserved seats, on the latest census – "one person, one vote, one value".

section: Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
sub: Delimitation – Commission, Freeze and Amendments
text: Members (2002 Act): a retired Supreme Court judge (chair), the CEC or an EC he nominates, and the State Election Commissioner – ex officio.

section: Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
sub: EVM-VVPAT, NOTA and Indelible Ink
text: EVM = electronic vote-recording and counting device (not an electoral system). First used: Parur (Kerala), 1982; older EVMs recorded up to 3,840 votes – current ECI EVMs up to 2,000.

text: AP's 13 Zilla Parishads are being reorganised into 28 (one per district) after their terms ended on 24 Sep 2026 (as of 2026).

text: 2026: 13 Zilla Praja Parishads reorganised into 28 (one per district); MPTC/ZPTC polls on 5 November 2026; SEC Anil Chandra Punetha ordered photo electoral rolls (as of Nov 2026).

text: Other 1991 numbers: fiscal deficit about 9.4% of GDP, inflation about 12%, GDP growth only about 1.3%.

section: Financial Regulators – Rbi, Sebi, Irdai, Pfrda, Ibbi, Ifsca – Mandate and Powers
sub: FSDC and FSLRC
text: FSDC (Financial Stability and Development Council), 2010: non-statutory apex body (executive order), not an organ of NITI Aayog; chaired by the Union Finance Minister (not RBI Governor); sub-committee chaired by the RBI Governor. Proposed by the Raghuram Rajan Committee (2008).

section: Financial Regulators – Rbi, Sebi, Irdai, Pfrda, Ibbi, Ifsca – Mandate and Powers
sub: FSDC and FSLRC
text: Roles: financial stability, inter-regulatory coordination, macro-prudential supervision, financial literacy and inclusion – not fixing the repo rate.
